title: Activation aliasing wraparound in hybrid kernel path causes token corruption and numerical drift
creator: Aisha Patel
description: A correctness regression appears when the serving runtime performs a speculative kernel promotion from tiled-attention to fused-attention during prefill->decode transitions under mixed-precision settings. The issue manifests as activation buffer aliasing (wraparound of a circular activation index) which leads to silent overwrites in the KV backing store and accumulating FP16 numerical drift over long prefixes. End result: token-level divergence (softmax instability) and occasional final-token corruption visible in regen tests.
steps_to_reproduce: Run the reproducer harness 'tests/repro/prefill_decode_activation_wrap' with model 'llama-2-7b' quantized to fp16 and an enforced kernel promotion at token index boundary 2048.
Use workload config: batch_size=6, seq_len_prefill=2048, decode_steps=64, continuous_batched=true, speculative_kernel_promotion=true.
Observe that the decoded token sequence diverges from baseline after ~40 decode steps and check runtime logs for "activation_index_wrap" warnings and KV-slot overwrite traces.
Run with env DEBUG_KV_SNAPSHOT=1 to emit KV contents at promotion boundary and compare across runs with/without speculative promotion.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (2025-11-05): Reproducer reliably fails in CI perf lab when kernel promotion path is forced; failure not observed when promotion disabled or when inputs are shorter than promotion boundary.
Heap/Memory check (2025-11-12): No OOM; corruption localized to KV slab logical contents rather than GPU memory faults.

Numerics analysis (2025-11-20): FP16 accumulation bias amplifies after aliasing event; reproduces deterministically with deterministic CUDA flags disabled, and also when using deterministic flags indicating ordering sensitivity.

Concurrency angle (2025-12-03): Race window occurs during handoff: prefill writes pending activations, scheduler triggers kernel promotion while decode path reads overlapping indices. Prefill finish handshake and promotion timer both compete to rotate the circular activation pointer.
Scheduler logs (2026-01-14): Found off-by-one in promotion code that uses <= boundary condition; with edge-case sequences this causes index to wrap to zero instead of advancing to boundary slot.
Patch experiment (2026-02-02): Adding an atomic compare-and-swap around pointer rotation eliminates overwrites but introduces a measurable tail latency regression (~0.9ms p50 for 2k prefills).
root_cause: A combination of an off-by-one index calculation in the speculative kernel promotion path and non-atomic rotation of the circular activation index. When a promotion is triggered at the exact prefill boundary, the index wraps to an aliasing slot while outstanding prefill writes are still completing, producing silent KV slot overwrites. The overwritten slots plus mixed-precision accumulation cause numerical drift that amplifies in the softmax and leads to token divergence.
proposed_fix: Primary: introduce a lightweight per-shard promotion barrier: mark target rotation slot as 'quiesce' and drain outstanding prefill writes before swapping the active index. Use atomic state flags to avoid full scheduler serialization.
Secondary: tighten boundary math to use exclusive upper-bound checks (prevent off-by-one).
Mitigation: add runtime assertion in debug builds to detect activation index overlap and emit actionable traces (KV snapshots + active-writer stack).
Performance tuning: implement a fast-path no-op for promotions when sequence lengths are significantly below boundary to avoid added latency for common short requests.
tests: Add unit test 'activation_wrap_edgecase' that fuzzes boundary values and asserts no slot overlap after promotion under hbatches and single-threaded and multi-threaded scheduler configs.
Add integration job to nightly CI that runs reproducer with both deterministic and non-deterministic CUDA flags to catch ordering-sensitive regressions.
Add e2e regen test comparing model outputs against baseline for 2k+ prefills with promotion forced on and off.
rollout_plan: Merge fix to canary runtime images in 'canary-region-us-west-2' and run perf + correctness sweep for 48 hours.
If canary passes correctness and latency targets, deploy to 10% traffic in hosted environment with promotion_enabled flag toggled via feature flag.
Monitor token-level divergence metric, per-model softmax-variance dashboard, and KV-snapshot assertion rate for 72 hours before full rollout.
Have rollback ready: revert pointer rotation commit and re-enable previous atomic CAS guard if unexpected customer impact observed.
observed_impacts: High-severity diffs in regen tests for long-context workloads (~3% top-1 token divergence on affected runs).
Intermittent customer reports of 'incoherent completions' for prompt templates with ~2k prefix tokens (reported by two enterprise customers).
Potential data integrity concern in Dedicated clusters where KV isolation expectations are strict; risk of cross-request contamination if not fixed.
